tob-10472: The Douay-Rheims Bible was the English Catholic answer to the King James Version, translated from the Latin Vulgate by scholars of the English College at Douai. This first half of the Old Testament runs from Genesis through Job in the stately wording later revised by Bishop Challoner. It gave English-speaking Catholics their own beloved translation of the Scriptures.
tob-0172: E. A. Wallis Budge’s famed rendering of the Egyptian Book of the Dead gives the spells for the soul’s hard road — past gate-wards and judges to the Field of Reeds. His notes and word-lists made the papyri speak to common readers. The book opened old Egypt’s afterlife to the modern mind.
tob-4172: Albert Schweitzer’s Quest knocked down a century of Jesus-lives, showing each learned man had painted the Master in his own likeness. His finding — that Jesus was a world’s-end prophet wrong about the end — closed an age of delving. The book is the most famed work of Bible-criticism ever penned.
tob-4072: George Grote’s History of Greece is the great Victorian telling of the ancient world, penned by a banker turned radical MP. This fifth volume spans the Periclean age and the Peloponnesian War in full. Grote’s love of democracy made Athens his hero. The work set the bar for Greek history in English.
cia-0000106272: A January 1965 situation report on the country of Laos, its subject line left untitled in the archive. These country sitreps summed up the military and political picture for officials who needed the whole story fast. Laos in 1965 meant a grinding shadow war, and this report is one more frame in that long, violent film.
cia-0000109072: A November 1967 report on views — source deleted by censors — concerning Fidel Castro and the prospects for revolution in Latin America. Someone's assessment of Castro's revolutionary export business was sensitive enough to hide the author's name. The redaction adds intrigue to an already sharp subject: was the revolution spreading or stalling?
cia-0000119172: A November 1967 report simply titled Guyana — the former British Guiana, a year into independence under Forbes Burnham. The single-word title suggests a country briefing: everything Washington needed to know, distilled. The document is a snapshot of a young nation already sliding toward authoritarian rule.
cia-0000124272: A November 1957 collection of miscellaneous comments on the first Soviet earth satellite's launching. Scientists, officials, and pundits all weighed in on Sputnik — awe, fear, and calculation. The document is the world's reaction, clipped and filed: the moment the space age felt real.
cia-0000126872: An August 1968 study of the military costs of the Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia. Crushing the Prague Spring took five armies and a fortune in fuel, pay, and logistics. The document prices the invasion — empire, itemized in rubles and manpower.
cia-0000126972: An estimated January 1975 document, title deleted, on Angola and China — concerning an Angolan delegation's visit, the truncated title suggests. Beijing backed its own Angolan faction, complicating the superpower chessboard. The censored title hides the details of China's African gambit.
cia-0000132272: Situation Report 578 with an oil slick update and more — the truncated title compresses the day's news. The spill kept spreading; the politics kept churning. The entry pairs environmental disaster with diplomacy: the war's two fronts, side by side.
cia-0000132572: An October 1960 report on the Cuban militia becoming an instrument of the police state. The revolution's armed citizens were turning into its enforcers. The document is the transformation: the militia, from defense to control.
cia-0000135872: A 1953 Guatemala general plan of action. The master plan for the coup, in outline. The document is the blueprint: the overthrow, designed.
cia-0000136272: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for LANGEVIN with instruction fourteen for broadcasts. The count continued in words. The entry is the instruction: the broadcasts, directed — fourteen.
cia-0000136972: A 1954 cable providing suggested actions in view of pro-Guatemala actions by local law-something — the truncated title cuts off the noun. The response, proposed. The document is the suggestion: the actions, listed.
cia-0000137472: An estimated 1961 document on President Kennedy's trip to Venezuela and Colombia. The December 1961 tour, previewed or reviewed. The document is the journey: the young president, south of the border.
cia-0000139372: NIE 12-61: the European satellites, 1961. The empire's edge, estimated. The document is the judgment: the satellites, surveyed.
cia-0000141172: A 1962 page from Juan Gonzalez's enlistment form. The recruit, on paper. The document is the form: the enlistment, filed.
un-ga-res-a-69-72: Resolution A/69/72, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The seventy-second act. The designation and year align; the subject belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-72: Security Council Resolution 72, adopted in 1949. The young Council at work. The designation and year are preserved; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-972: Security Council Resolution 972, cataloged with the year 1992 — the numbering suggests 1995, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1172: Security Council Resolution 1172, adopted in June 1998 — the nuclear tests resolution, condemning India and Pakistan's underground tests and demanding they stop. The subcontinent's arms race drew the world's censure. The resolution is the condemnation: the tests, deplored.
un-sc-res-1572: Security Council Resolution 1572, cataloged with the year 2005 — the historical record places this Côte d'Ivoire sanctions resolution in November 2004, imposing an arms embargo over the civil war. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000132672: A 1961 CIA paper titled Is Time on Our Side in Cuba, numbered 0000132672. The question hung over Washington as the revolution hardened. The document is the question: the clock, doubted.
cia-0000132772: A 1960 CIA Cuba developments file — number 0000132772. The series continued. The document is the series: the developments, filed.
cia-0000134272: A 1959 CIA file titled The Situation in Cuba, numbered 0000134272. The revolution's first year — Batista had just fled. The document is the beginning: the situation, brand new.
cia-0000136772: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136772. The training year's papers, firm-dated. The document is the training: the papers, early.
cia-0000139172: A 1979 CIA file of excerpts from a daily dairy — number 0000139172. The next year's excerpts. The document is the next: the diary, continued.
un-ga-res-a-60-472: General Assembly Resolution A/60/472, cataloged with the year 2006 — the numbering suggests 2005-2006, roughly aligned. The designation and year are preserved; the subject belongs to the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d72: A memorandum by the Secretary of State, October 29, 1943 — Document 72. The department's thinking, recorded. The memo is the record: the secretary, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d172: The Secretary of State to the President, October 30, 1943 — Document 172. The department briefed the White House. The memo is the briefing: the secretary, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d272: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 272. The editors' link. The note is the link: the chain, unbroken.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d372: Ware minutes — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 372. Another notetaker's record of the Tehran talks. The minutes are Ware's: the talks, captured.
arxiv-2605-08672: Physics-informed neural networks solve differential equations by baking physical laws into the training loss, and the Bayesian version also reports how sure it is. Yuxuan Zhao and Yulong Lu prove that for elliptic partial differential equations, the posterior concentrates — uncertainty shrinks — around the true solution as data grows. The 2026 paper supplies the theoretical guarantee the popular method was missing.
arxiv-2605-08872: Turbulence remains physics' great unsolved mess, and engineers model it with approximations called closures. Fu Yujie, Zhang Yihan, Deng Wanru, and Dai Yuanjun learn symbolic closures from data — readable equations, not black boxes — inside the lattice Boltzmann framework. The 2026 paper aims at turbulence models that are both accurate and interpretable.
arxiv-2605-09272: A medical AI that sees scans, hears symptoms, and talks back is the dream of the clinic. Meet Shah, Jason Gusdorf, Anil Palepu, and colleagues work toward conversational medical AI with eyes, ears, and a voice. The 2026 paper sketches the multimodal doctor's assistant.
arxiv-2605-09372: Martingale square functions measure the accumulated wobble of a random process, and weighted norm estimates bound them precisely. Wei Chen, Yong Jiao, Xingyan Quan, and Lian Wu prove sharp versions of these estimates. The 2026 paper is harmonic analysis at its most precise.
arxiv-2605-09472: Attention with linear position biases is powerful and expensive; locality-sensitive hashing can cheapen it dramatically. Daniel Wolfson and Tal Wagner approximate the biased attention with binary block matrices — Positional LSH. The 2026 paper makes biased attention affordable at real-world scale.
arxiv-2605-09772: Exploring an unknown nonlinear process is risky — one wrong move can break the physical system. S. Tonini, S. Rastegarpour, H. R. Feyzmahdavian, and colleagues explore safely using online Gaussian process learning. The 2026 paper is cautious control theory with uncertainty quantified.
plos-pone-0003372: Laboratory chemists solved a practical measurement headache in this 2008 anesthesia paper. The anesthetic isoflurane evaporates so fast that its true concentration in open lab dishes is hard to pin down. By pairing concentration checks with electrical recordings of nerve synapses, the team built a method for getting honest dose-response data from volatile anesthetics.
plos-pone-0003472: Biologist Kenneth Catania solved a folk mystery in this 2008 paper: why vibrating a wooden stake in Florida soil summons earthworms. Worm grunters, who harvest the giant native Diplocardia worms for bait, unknowingly mimic the vibrations of burrowing moles, the worms' predators. Fleeing what they mistake for a hunter, the worms surface straight into the harvesters' hands.
plos-pone-0003572: Geneticists found parental origin matters differently by tissue in this 2008 mouse study. Crossing two deer-mouse species produced hybrids where imprinting, the silencing of one parent's gene copy, failed in patterns that varied by tissue and gene cluster. The patchwork reveals that imprinting is regulated locally, not by one genome-wide rule.
plos-pone-0003672: In 2008, Riehle, Xu, and Lazzaro found the mosquito's anti-malaria arsenal. The APL1 gene family in Anopheles gambiae, built from variable leucine-rich repeat proteins, proved needed for Rel1-driven defense against the malaria parasite. The finding names the insect immune genes that decide whether a bite transmits disease.
plos-pone-0003772: Mazzaccara, Labruna, and Cito published the mouse lab manual in this 2008 paper. They measured age-related reference ranges for the main blood chemistry and cell counts in three common lab mouse strains. The baseline tables let researchers spot real disease effects instead of normal variation.
plos-pone-0003872: In 2008, Polymenidou, Moos, and Scott assembled a full antibody arsenal against prions. Their POM monoclonals cover non-overlapping epitopes of the prion protein, giving researchers a complete toolkit. The comprehensive set speeds both diagnosis and basic prion research.
plos-pone-0003972: In 2008, Banks, d'Errico, and Peterson blamed competition for the Neanderthals' end. Their models showed modern humans outcompeting Neanderthals for the same resources and land. Climate change alone could not explain the extinction pattern as well as rivalry could. The competitive-exclusion case makes our cousins' disappearance a story of losing out.
plos-pone-0004072: In 2008, Reiner, Krasnov-Yoeli, and Dehtiar gave an old enzyme a new job. A chromatin-bound form of RNase P drove efficient transcription by RNA polymerase III. The tRNA-processing enzyme moonlighted as a transcription helper. The double life rewrites RNase P's textbook role.
plos-pone-0004172: In 2009, Boo, Song, and Kim linked a protein pileup to cell death. Built-up phospho-beta-catenin worsened ROS-driven death in cells missing presenilin. The protein backlog turned oxidative stress lethal. The link ties presenilin to cell survival. Clearing the backlog could rescue vulnerable cells.
plos-pone-0004272: In 2009, Sapin, Lapray, and Berod mapped the brain's dream switch. Brainstem GABAergic neurons controlling REM sleep were precisely pinpointed. The paradoxical-sleep circuit's brakes were located. The new map advances sleep neuroscience greatly. The neurons silence muscles while the brain dreams.
plos-pone-0358872: Cracks in bridges start small and grow deadly — and inspecting every span by hand is slow. This paper presents Yolov8-CA-EYHL, an improved AI vision algorithm that spots cracks in bridge images automatically. Built on the YOLOv8 detection framework with added attention modules, it aims to make infrastructure inspections faster, cheaper, and more reliable.
plos-pone-0342672: Viruses engineered to kill cancer cells can team up with chemotherapy — if the doses and timing are right. This paper built a quantitative treatment model to optimize combined virotherapy-chemotherapy regimens against HPV-driven cervical cancer. The math finds the schedule that kills the most cancer with the least harm.
plos-pone-0356872: Smallholder forests in Indonesia’s Ciamis Regency store carbon — but how much depends on what grows there. This paper measured tree diversity and standing carbon stocks, testing effects of cropping patterns and elevation. The results show which farming patterns keep both biodiversity and carbon high.
plos-pone-0358772: ALS patients can silently retain carbon dioxide as breathing weakens. This paper found that the serum Na-Cl value — sodium minus chloride from routine blood tests — reflects CO2 retention in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. A number doctors already have could become an early warning for respiratory failure.
plos-pone-0350972: A railway from China to Thailand rewrites trade maps. This paper measured the effect of the China-Thailand railway on Thailand’s trade with China’s Guangxi Province. The trade shifts it documented show how infrastructure redraws economic geography.
plos-pone-0358572: Fabry disease hides in plain sight — and broader gene panels are finally finding it. This paper examined how including the GLA gene in wider NGS/WES panels changed the known phenotypic spectrum of Fabry disease. The shifting landscape shows the disease is more varied — and more common — than once thought.
plos-pone-0358472: Psoriasis and metabolic syndrome travel together far too often — and they share genes. This paper mapped their shared genetic basis and built a spatial cellular atlas spanning both conditions. The atlas shows exactly where the two diseases’ biology overlaps, cell by cell and tissue by tissue.
plos-pone-0343472: Trusting AI means understanding it — especially inscrutable large language models. This paper proposed hybrid explainable AI approaches for interpreting LLMs, bridging the gap between trust and performance. The hybrid explanations aim to make giant models legible to the humans who must rely on them.
plos-pone-0357272: Buses that brake themselves must balance crash avoidance with passenger comfort — nobody wants riders thrown. This paper designed an optimal coordination control strategy for autonomous emergency braking in commercial buses, weighing safety against comfort. The strategy stops the bus hard without turning the cabin into a hazard.
plos-pone-0357772: Tuberculosis with lung cavities on chest X-ray may need longer treatment to stay cured. This paper studied extended treatment duration and recurrence in successfully treated drug-susceptible pulmonary TB with cavities. The findings inform one of TB care’s most practical questions: how long is long enough?
plos-pone-0357572: Stress derails diets — not in general, but moment by moment. This protocol plans intensive longitudinal assessment of stress and stress-related concepts across a weight loss program, using ecological momentary assessment on phones. The planned data will capture stress exactly as dieters live it, in real time.
plos-pone-0356072: Where do neighbors actually meet in disadvantaged Dutch neighborhoods? This qualitative participatory study looked through different lenses at meeting places — assessing needs, barriers, and successes with residents themselves. The community voices offer urban planners a grounded guide to renewal that people will use.
plos-pone-0345072: Poetry moves listeners through sound as much as sense — and the effect crosses languages. This cross-linguistic investigation showed prosody can shape and modulate listeners’ emotional experience of poetry beyond semantics. The human voice carries feeling in its rhythm and melody, whatever the words mean.
plos-pone-0357672: Acidic electrolyzed oxidizing water is a useful disinfectant — but identifying it quickly used to require a lab. This lighthouse-shaped rapid identification device detects it through conductivity differences: a genuinely low-cost method. The clever design democratizes quality testing for small producers.
plos-pone-0352372: Crohn’s disease starves the body even when patients eat. This cross-sectional study compared multidimensional nutritional assessment between active disease and remission. The detailed comparison guides nutritional care — showing clinicians what to measure and when to intervene.
plos-pone-0357372: Pain control after total laparoscopic hysterectomy shapes recovery profoundly. This paper tested the efficacy of different oliceridine doses for patient-controlled intravenous analgesia after the procedure. The dosing data help anesthesiologists optimize relief while minimizing opioid side effects.
plos-pone-0342872: Obstetric referrals in Addis Ababa’s public health centers can mean life or death — yet the system creaks. This mixed-methods study examined referral practices and the health system factors shaping them. The findings expose bottlenecks that cost mothers and babies precious time.
plos-pone-0356172: Quantum computers are scarce — but FPGAs can emulate them. This paper presented an FPGA-based emulation framework for two-qubit quantum computation, covering design, implementation, and validation. The framework gives researchers and students hands-on quantum experience without a quantum computer.
plos-pone-0356472: Can a satellite image predict a neighborhood’s health and wealth? This paper asked whether a satellite image is worth a thousand data points, comparing machine learning approaches to predict environmental and social inequalities across England. The comparison reveals how much inequality is literally visible from space.
plos-pone-0356272: Steel wire ropes — holding up elevators, cranes, and bridges — develop surface defects that precede catastrophic failure. WireGC-Former segments those defects from 3D point clouds. The AI inspector sees damage human eyes miss — promising earlier warnings before ropes snap.
plos-pone-0355872: Caring for someone with severe, persistent mental illness exhausts caregivers — in body, mind, and spirit. This Saudi study examined caregiver burden and its association with depression, anxiety, and quality of life. The findings demand that mental health systems care for the carers, not just the patients.
plos-pone-0352872: Americans choosing childfree lives cluster geographically — but does state context explain it? This paper mapped the spatial distribution of the U.S. childfree population and tested whether state context matters. The findings reveal how policy climates — from abortion access to childcare — shape one of life’s biggest decisions.
plos-pone-0355372: 5G small cells must hand off users seamlessly as they move. This paper proposed a mobility and resource prediction method for seamless handover and service continuity. The predictive approach keeps calls and data flowing as users dart between tiny cells — the invisible choreography of next-generation wireless.
plos-pone-0355472: Wolfberry — goji — polysaccharides differ depending on how they’re extracted. This paper compared non-thermally extracted polysaccharides from fresh berries against conventionally extracted ones from dried berries. The comparison reveals whether gentle extraction preserves the bioactive compounds that make goji prized.
plos-pone-0355672: Daidzin — a soybean compound — might fight breast cancer through multiple molecular targets. This paper mapped its mechanisms via network pharmacology and multi-level molecular modeling. The computational pharmacology modernizes soy’s folk reputation with precise molecular hypotheses worth testing.
europmc-pmc2796172: Hepatitis C virus rewires the liver cells it infects, and this 2010 paper tracks exactly how. By profiling proteins and fats over time, the authors reveal the virus reprogramming the cell's metabolism and energy production to serve its own replication. The detailed map exposes metabolic weak points that future antiviral drugs might target.
europmc-pmc2799472: Flame-stopping chemicals build up in the body, and this 2009 paper follows children who met them before birth. The team tested the children's motion, thought, and conduct at school age against gauged levels in the womb. Exposed children scored worse in each area. The results built the case for curbing such chemicals in home goods.
europmc-pmc2805672: Healthy mouths share a common set of microbes, and this 2009 paper tries to define it. The authors sequence oral bacterial communities to identify the core microbiome found in most healthy people. Knowing the normal baseline makes it possible to spot the shifts that come with gum disease and cavities. The study set a reference point for oral health research.
europmc-pmc2826372: Aphids are major crop pests with bizarre biology, and this 2010 paper delivers their genetic blueprint. The International Aphid Genomics Consortium presents the genome sequence of the pea aphid, Acyrthosiphon pisum. The landmark sequence revealed strange features, including genes borrowed from fungi. It opened aphid biology to genomic investigation.
europmc-pmc2837572: Inflammation can push cancer cells to migrate, and this 2010 review traces the signaling chain. The authors describe the TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/Snail pathway that drives cancer cell migration and invasion. Their overview connects immune signals to metastasis. The pathway became a candidate target for stopping cancer spread.
europmc-pmc2841772: Premature birth and stillbirth devastate families worldwide, yet data remain patchy. This 2010 global report, first in a series of seven, defines the terms, describes the burden, and identifies opportunities to improve data. The authors set the measurement agenda. The report became the baseline for tracking progress on newborn survival.
europmc-pmc2871172: Carving up habitats kills species now and later. This 2010 paper shows fragmentation causes immediate and time-delayed biodiversity loss across food-chain levels. The authors' field work reveals the lag between damage and disappearance. Their finding warns that today's fragments hold tomorrow's extinctions.
europmc-pmc2874872: Brain zaps can calm Parkinson's shakes when drugs fall short. This 2010 trial pits deep brain stimulation plus best drugs against drugs alone for advanced Parkinson's. The authors' randomized test favored the combo. Their result cemented stimulation as a mainstay for severe cases.
europmc-pmc2877672: Electronic cigarettes were brand new in 2010, and this paper asked who was using them and why. The author surveys e-cigarette users, their habits, and motives. The early snapshot informed regulators facing a novel product. The study captured vaping at its dawn.
europmc-pmc2883572: Treating HIV widely may cut new infections citywide. This 2010 San Francisco study shows drops in community viral load came with fewer new HIV infections. The authors' data backed treatment as prevention in a real city. Their finding helped sell test-and-treat strategies around the world.
europmc-pmc2965572: Cataract genes needed a map, and this 2010 paper draws it. The authors present Cat-Map, a database putting cataract genes on the map for researchers. Their resource speeds eye genetics work. The tool became a reference for lens scientists. It links each gene to its disease story.
europmc-pmc2981572: Gene lists need pictures, and this 2010 paper draws them. The authors bring Enrichment Map, a network tool that turns gene-set results into readable maps. Their software untangles crowded tables. The tool became a lab staple. Researchers cite it in thousands of studies.
europmc-pmc2996072: Tiny metal bits promise big medical payoffs. This 2010 review introduces metal nanoparticles and their many uses. The authors survey how labs make and test them. Their overview opened a fast-growing field. Cancer, imaging, and drug delivery all benefit. Safety questions still shadow the hype.
europmc-pmc3004072: Hip fractures vary wildly around the world. This 2011 review maps where hip breaks strike most and least. The authors reveal stark geographic patterns. Their work guides bone health policy. Northern countries bear the heaviest burden. Vitamin D and lifestyle explain part of the gap.
europmc-pmc3046172: Kids' noses host diverse germs. This 2011 paper takes a gene census of nose germs in children. The authors reveal the nasal roster. Their work aids vaccine science. Vaccinated kids carried different germ mixes. Ear infection bugs lurk in the mix.
europmc-pmc3088472: Beetle family names got cataloged. This 2011 paper lists every family-group name in the beetle order. The authors' giant list steadies naming. Their work aids beetle scientists. Thousands of names made the cut. The catalog settles old naming fights. Museums relabel drawers with it.
europmc-pmc6631472: Kaempferol - a plant flavonoid in kale, beans, and tea - keeps showing anti-cancer promise in the lab. This review gathers the evidence: how the compound slows tumor growth across breast, bone, cervical, and other cancers. The authors make the case for taking this dietary molecule seriously as a chemopreventive.
europmc-pmc6669472: Many viruses first grab heparan sulfate - sugary chains bristling on cell surfaces - before invading. This review asks whether these proteoglycans are true receptors or just convenient handholds that lab-grown viruses evolved to exploit. The answer reshapes how we think about viral entry.
europmc-pmc6751072: Mental illness may smolder with inflammation - but the evidence is scattered. This cross-disorder study tested inflammation-related blood markers across major psychiatric diagnoses for reproducibility. The assessment separates robust signals from noise, guiding where immune-targeted psychiatry should go next.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-72: This 2007 GAO report finds the Energy Department dragging its feet on rounding up bomb-grade material — plutonium and hot uranium strewn across its sites. Years after pledging to lock it down, GAO said, little had moved. The report presses the department to hurry on one of the gravest housekeeping jobs on earth.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1172: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report on climate-change research data: agencies had data-sharing policies but could do more to make federally funded research data available. Taxpayer-paid science was not always reaching other scientists or the public. GAO's findings press agencies to open up the data behind climate research so findings can be checked, reused, and built upon.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1072: The Pentagon's business side needed a single throat to choke — GAO's 2007 report says only a chief management officer could bring focus. Reform energy kept scattering across the brass. The findings argue for one empowered leader to drag the world's largest bureaucracy into shape.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-772: Washington's road money was loosening up in 2007 — GAO's report finds flexible funding let states and towns chase their own transport priorities. The findings praise the multi-use dollars while watching for drift. The report frames flexibility as trust: let locals pave where the potholes are.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-572: Retiree drug coverage was holding on in 2007 — GAO's report says most sponsors kept offering prescription benefits and picked the federal subsidy option. The findings map the employer choices in detail. The report captures the moment before the retiree-health tide turned for good.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-272: Enrolling the poorest in drug plans stayed hard in 2007 — GAO's report details the hurdles facing the dual-eligible at every step. The findings map the enrollment maze from start to finish. The report asks why the neediest faced the steepest paperwork of all.
gao-gaoreports-b-299072: Hydroid LLC took its January 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Underwater-tech deals get the same surface-level fairness.
openalex-w7206150172: Brazil's constitution bans evidence gathered by illegal means. But what if that evidence would prove the accused person innocent? This law article studies the rare case for letting such evidence in when it helps the defense. The authors weigh legal principles against the risk of jailing someone who did nothing wrong. A technical but high-stakes debate about when fairness to the accused should outweigh the rule against tainted proof.
openalex-w7207663672: Children can learn to save lives, including the Heimlich maneuver for choking. This integrative review asks what teaching methods actually work for basic life support skills in school-age kids, looking at hands-on practice, knowledge gained, and confidence in an emergency. The authors pull together studies on first-aid education for children. The message is encouraging: with the right approach, even young students can learn to respond when seconds count.
openalex-w7204627872: Could your morning coffee protect your brain? This integrative review looks at evidence that caffeine may shield against Parkinson's disease by blocking certain brain receptors. The authors gather studies on the compound's possible protective role as the disease grows more common. Cautious but intriguing, it reviews a humble drink's potential as brain medicine.
openalex-w7204260272: Obstetric violence, mistreatment during pregnancy and childbirth, is finally being named and fought. This article studies the movement defending women who suffered such abuse: its legal wins, its hurdles, and its place in public health. The authors frame the struggle as a matter of justice, not just medicine. A rights-based look at dignity in the delivery room.
openalex-w4412377772: Bird flocks inspired a famous model, and this paper sorts its clusters. The authors combined the Vicsek flocking model with DBSCAN, a data-clustering algorithm, to map the model's cluster phases. They charted how groups form as parameters change. A computational study where birds meet big data.
openalex-w7128094572: The immune system tells friend from foe with astonishing precision. This educational paper explains how T-cell receptors and MHC molecules, the HLA system, create that diversity. The authors walked through the recognition machinery. An immunology primer on the body's ID-check system.
openalex-w4410198872: Diabetes keeps spreading as insulin-making cells fail. This review covers beta-cell breakdown in the pancreas: how these cells falter and blood sugar climbs. The authors surveyed the damage routes. A hormone review of the tiny cells at the heart of diabetes.
pmc-13453072: A 2026 medicinal chemistry paper creating new organometallic — metal-containing — derivatives of benzimidazole deworming drugs and testing them against parasites. Adding metal centers to known anthelmintics can change how they kill. The study reports the synthesis and the antiparasitic activity of the new compounds.
pmc-13429372: This 2026 paper describes and evaluates a pragmatic family program designed to meet education and support needs in early psychosis. When psychosis first strikes, families are often lost; structured support changes outcomes. The evaluation shows what the program achieved and where it can improve.
pmc-13554772: A 2026 cardiology study examining how kidney function predicts prognosis in non-ST-elevation heart attacks, with and without percutaneous coronary intervention. Kidney disease complicates every cardiac decision, and the study quantifies the trade-offs. The results guide treatment choices in a common, tricky population.
pmc-13418372: A 2026 population study of 3,066 people asking whether ABO blood type affects immune response and vaccine efficacy after COVID-19 booster shots. Blood group effects on infection have been debated since 2020. The large sample gives one of the clearer answers.
pmc-13354872: A 2026 cardiology paper showing that mitoquinone — a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant — prevents cardiac dysfunction after heart attack by normalizing mitochondrial ROS and calcium handling. Targeting the powerhouse directly protected the heart. The mechanism supports mitochondria-first therapy for MI.
pmc-13429872: This 2026 ESHRE position paper sets international limits on the number of offspring per gamete donor. Donor-conceived families and regulators need clear boundaries. The position paper gives the field a shared standard.
pmc-13487472: In this 2026 leukemia paper, molecular glues targeting LCK — a key signaling protein — overcame resistance to inhibitor-based therapy in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. When inhibitors stop working, glues that degrade the target offer a way around. The study demonstrates the strategy in a hard-to-treat blood cancer.
pmc-13481672: This 2026 six-country study examined how civil society organizations and academia participated in COVID-19 governance. Pandemic response wasn't just governments. The comparative insights show what inclusive governance looked like.
pmc-13431672: In this 2026 infectious disease paper, declining moxifloxacin efficacy against Mycoplasma genitalium raised the question: is it time for resistance-guided therapy? The STI is outrunning the drug. The paper argues for testing before treating.
pmc-13469072: In this 2026 agricultural paper, artificial domestication of Gleditsia sinensis (honey locust) traded yield against quality — phenotypic and functional variation in a common garden. Breeding for more changed the chemistry. The trade-off is the lesson.
pmc-13424772: A 2026 primer on artificial intelligence for palliative care educators. AI is entering end-of-life care. The primer prepares the teachers.
pmc-13437072: This 2026 Alberta retrospective cohort study compared acute outcomes of robotic versus laparoscopic and open hysterectomy for endometrial cancer. The surgical approaches were head-to-head. The cohort data inform the choice.
